head.lede: There are exactly five kinds of why. They are ranked, and the ranking decides everything.

theLittleLanguage.title: There is no regex engine
lede: Not “we avoided regex”: the core is allowed
outside dependencies, so there is nothing to have a regex engine with. Instead the four-part shape from tier 4 was written down once, and every provider detector is an instance of it.

cards.title: What that buys
body: No backtracking exists, so the classic one-evil-input-hangs-the-server attack has nowhere to live,
rather than by review. A lookup table computed once per scan keeps the whole pass linear, even on hostile input.

cards.title: What it costs
cards.body: Anything that is not “prefix, then a bounded run” needs hand-written code. Two vendors' formats needed exactly that.

bringYourOwnRules.title: Your format, their engine
lede: Companies have their own key formats. Adding a detector used to mean writing Rust, so everyone else ran a second scan of their own beside this one, which is exactly the divergence the library exists to prevent. Now you hand over the same four-part shape as plain text. Not a callback:
